Public evidence summary (no measured savings claimed).

1) Task s19g_taco-test-670 (string/character-count construction; stages l3 and l4): both events WRONG_ANSWER on the 6-case input "6
4 2
baba
5 2
baacb
5 3
baacb
5 3
aaaaa
6 4
aaxxzz
7 1
phoenix
". Expected first line "ab"; actual first line "aa"; remaining five lines match. Both codes are the same 1181-byte fragment (identical sha256), truncated mid-statement at "distinct = s", so the observed wrong first line may be an artifact of incomplete code. Condition: do not conclude the counting logic is wrong from these events. Uncertainty: root cause not established. Stop rule: do not claim a fix or savings for this task without a complete-code run.

2) Task s19g_taco-train-s00-r1653 (cube-state / move-cycle simulation; stages l3 and l4): both events WRONG_ANSWER on the 24-integer input "2 5 4 6 1 3 6 2 5 5 1 2 3 5 3 1 1 2 4 6 6 4 3 4
". Expected "NO" (2 bytes); actual "NO
" (3 bytes). Outputs match textually apart from trailing newline, so the mismatch may be formatting/whitespace or a harness artifact; treat as unresolved. Both codes are fragments (1488 and 1722 bytes) truncated mid-comment at "A cyc". Condition: the near-match does not prove correctness. Uncertainty: root cause not established.

Cross-cutting rules: All events are stage l3/l4 with fragments; no complete, verified solution appears in this evidence. Do not invent measured savings, speedups, or pass rates. Do not assert a root cause beyond what the outputs show. Refuse to claim any task is solved. Stop: if asked to generalize from these fragments to a full solution, decline and request complete code plus a clean run.
